content.text:
Fixed. The second crash was a different limit: Slack caps the message text at 40,000 characters, and the fallback text the adapter derives from the card grows with every block, so a full data dump blew past it even though the individual blocks were valid.

What I changed in this round, in `apps/backend/src/utils/messaging-provider.ts`:

- `createSlackCard` now enforces a total budget, not just the 50-block cap. It walks the blocks from the newest backwards, measuring each one with the adapter's own fallback-text helper, and stops at 50 blocks or 30,000 characters, prepending a note that the start of the response was trimmed and can be read in nao. Keeping the tail means the final answer survives and the older tool-call chatter is what gets dropped.
- `formatSlackMessageText` (used for the plain `chat.postMessage` path from automations) truncates at the same budget.

I verified with three worst-case payloads — a 5,000-line CSV inside a code fence, a 5,000-row markdown table, and 400 paragraphs of prose. All three now produce at most 11 blocks, no section over 3,000 characters, a ~28 KB payload, and a fallback text under 28,000 characters. Previously the code-fence dump alone generated 164,000 characters of fallback text, which is exactly the `msg_too_long` you hit.

Together with the earlier fix (empty table cells, streaming partial rows, 99-row/10,000-character table caps), the tests are at 18 cases in `apps/backend/tests/slack-message-blocks.test.ts`, and `npm run lint` plus the Slack suites pass.

One thing worth deciding separately: for prompts like "return everything", the answer is now truncated with a pointer back to nao. The Slack bot already has `uploadFiles`, so an alternative would be to attach the full result as a CSV whenever a table gets truncated. Say the word and I'll wire that up.

Checking the truncation limits — `formatSlackMessageText` caps at 30,000 which is under Slack's 40,000 text limit, and the error handling in `_handleWorkFlow` now bounds the catch path to prevent huge errors from breaking the edit. Teams uses a different function so it's unaffected, and the only remaining edge case is the `chat` lib's markdown text posting, which should be minimal.

The root cause was unbounded fallback text and blocks, so now the card maxes out at 50 blocks and 30k characters with a trim note. I should also suggest a follow-up for large data requests — instead of truncating, users could upload a CSV file to Slack using the existing `uploadFiles` function, which would be cleaner than cutting off content.
